newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Human rights group slams arms sales to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Human rights group slams arms sales to Turkey.

text.p: A human rights groups said on Wednesday Turkey was planning to buy over 100 attack aircraft this year, further escalating tension over arms sales in the region.

The Washington-based Human Rights Watch said in a statement released in Belgium that Turkey was pressing ahead with plans to buy 50 Black hawk and four Chinook helicopters from the U.S., 30 Cougar helicopters from a French-German consortium and 54 Phantom F-4 jet upgrades from Israel.

Human Rights Watch -- which says it has documented the use of attack aircraft against Turkey's minority Kurd population -- said the purchases would contravene U.S. and Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe calls prohibiting such sales.
The organisation said it was basing its report on statements made by Turkish government officials and media sources.

"Human Rights Watch and other independent organisations have documented the use of fighter planes and military helicopters ... in Turkey's counter-insurgency campaign that has resulted in gross violations of international law," the statement said.
"This has included firing indiscriminately at villages ... killing civilians and destroying property, transporting troops to and from villages which are forcibly depopulated and burned."

Human Rights Watch said the PKK -- the Kurdish Workers Party group fighting for self rule in southeast Turkey -- was also implicated in "a pattern of human rights abuses such as extrajudicial killings, indiscriminate fire, kidnappings and extortion".
A Turkish embassy official was not immediately available for comment.
Human Rights Watch said the Turkish government was negotiating to buy the following:
-- four CH-47 Chinook military cargo helicopters made by Boeing in the U.S. and costing around $135 million;

-- 50 S-70A Black hawk armed transport helicopters, part of a $1.1 billion deal signed with U.S. manufacturer Sikorsky in 1992 for 95 helicopters. Turkey has already recieved 45 helicopters but the remainder of the deal has been suspended over a disagreement on co-production rights.
-- 30 AS-532 Cougar combat search and rescue and utility helicopters worth around $400 million from the French-German consortium Eurocopter.
-- 54 F-4 Phantom jet upgrades worth $600 million from Israel Aircraft Industries.
A row erupted last week over revelations that Cyprus was planning to buy S-300 anti-aircraft missiles from Russia in a deal that would compromise Turkish air superiority in the region.

The purchase angered Ankara which has long been at odds with Greece over control of divided Cyprus, invaded in 1974 by Turkey in response to a coup inspired by the then-ruling military junta in Athens.
Turkey and Greece nearly came to blows a year ago over disputed Aegean islets and clashes on Cyprus in the summer left five people dead.
